findings: start: pgrep -c headless_shell = 18, loadavg 10.59 - ABOVE the cap of 8, authoring phase first, browser verification deferred

ACTOR CENSUS, all 336 records with a `topics` array, counted off game/data/npcs/*.json: townsman 72, villager 37, legionary 31, rootkeeper 30, merchant 29, healer 29, dres-factor 25, clerk 20, innkeeper 19, mudborn 12, fisher 10, town-elder 9, sapcutter 4, outlaw 2, archivist 2, naga-elder 2, mercenary 2, deep-elder 1. EIGHTEEN names.

THE SIX ARCHETYPES (speakers.json) ARE NOT THE SAME SET AS THE ACTOR NAMES. Of the six -- rootkeeper, magister, sapcutter, archivist, mudborn, legionary -- `magister` HAS ZERO NPC RECORDS. Its province-side counterpart is the actor `dres-factor` (25 records), which answers nothing. So one of the six voices in speakers.json is written for a mouth that does not exist in the world, and the mouth that does exist has no lines. 31+30+12+4+2 = 79 answerable, which is exactly the 79 W1-26 measured.

THE UNANSWERED ARE ELEVEN NAMES, NOT TEN (the brief says ten): townsman 72, merchant 29, healer 29, dres-factor 25, innkeeper 19, fisher 10, town-elder 9, outlaw 2, naga-elder 2, mercenary 2, deep-elder 1 = 200 exactly. The 200 figure is right; the name count is 11.

NEW DEFECT, MINE, NOT PREVIOUSLY NAMED: `info.cell` IS READ BY NOTHING. infoAllowed() in converse.js checks requires/forbids/d/knows and never cell; the specificity score is (matchesActor?8)+(requires?4)+dScore+(forbids?0.5) and cell is not in it. 00-roots.json authors `cell` on 39 infos. Consequence measured below: a legionary standing in Thorn answers `specific place` with the STORMHOLD line, because among three legionary infos all scoring 8 the first authored wins. Every settlement-specific root answer in the game is currently delivered in the wrong town to everybody except the town it was written for. This is a model with no reader, RI-MTH07, one layer under the headline gap.

THE READER ALREADY HAS THE TWO-TIER SHAPE THE FIX NEEDS. converse.js infoFor(): `if (!matchesActor && info.a) continue` -- an info with `a` is locked to that actor; an info with NO `a` is usable by anyone and scores 0 against an actor-match's 8. So the generic tier exists and is EMPTY across all nine roots. The hole is not that the reader cannot express `most people say the same thing and a few say better`; it is that nobody wrote the `most people` half.

MEASURED THROUGH THE LIVE READER, BEFORE: 133 of 336 speakers could answer any root, not the 136 W1-26 reported. The three-person difference is DISPOSITION: W1-26's census did not pass one, so `d`-gated infos all opened. 1 rootkeeper and 2 mudborn sit below their own archetype's `d` bar. Pass the speaker's real base disposition and the honest before-figure is 133.

THE CELL DEFECT, CONFIRMED AND FIXED. 267 of the 1,065 infos in game/data/dialogue/topics/** carry `cell` and NOTHING read it. Turning the gate on moved `specific-place` from 133 answerable to 88 (people who only ever had another town's line now correctly get none) and its DISTINCT answers from 7 to 9 — all nine settlement lines became reachable in their own town, where before only three could ever fire whatever town you stood in. BLAST RADIUS across every non-root topic: own-topic offers 332 -> 329, records offering zero topics 155 -> 155. Three lines lost, seven towns' worth of wrong answers removed.
AFTER: coverage 133 -> 336 of 336. All EIGHTEEN actor names answer all nine roots (mean 9.00 each). DULLNESS 28.9% against a 60% ceiling. 736 cell-gated answers delivered, 0 misplaced.

THE INSTRUMENT WENT RED FIRST AND FOR THE RIGHT REASONS. Before the fix --self-test was 2 pass / 3 fail: M1 (strip the generic tier) could not move coverage BECAUSE THERE WAS NO GENERIC TIER, and M4 declared its own place check VACUOUS rather than passing on zero cell-gated deliveries. Both now pass.

MY OWN M3 MUTATION WAS BROKEN AND LOOKED LIKE A BROKEN METRIC. It filtered topics on `t.root`, but only the DECLARING file carries that flag — buildTopicIndex ORs it onto the merged record so 06-opening-roots and 07-root-coverage add root infos without re-declaring it. So the mutation missed the villager and clerk halves entirely and plateaued at 51.9% instead of 100%. Take the root roster off the INDEX, never off a file.

THE SPELLING SPLIT HAD EXACTLY THREE SITES: topic-supply.js RUMOUR_TOPIC, engine.js rumourFor() (which hardcoded the string rather than using the constant), and a regex in tools/quests/utility-findability.mjs. Every authored data file already used the root spelling.

AND FOLDING THE SPELLING EXPOSED A SECOND BUG IT HAD BEEN HIDING: Conversation.start() pushes every `extra` onto the list with no dedup. While the two spellings were distinct that produced two keywords for one subject; once folded it would have produced the SAME keyword twice in one list. Extras now REPLACE a matching list entry, which is also the right precedence — say() resolves extras first, so what the town is actually saying beats the province-wide 'ask at the inn'.

PROSE: the file failed tools/check-prose.mjs on first draft — sting 42.19 (ceiling 6.0), contractions 661 (band top 365), 9 `-body` forms, zero conjunction openers. SIX stings, all of the same shape: a closing 'That's the ...' recast. Flattened by hand, and the contraction overshoot cut by un-contracting the FORMAL voices only (dres-factor, naga-elder, deep-elder, town-elder, healer) rather than sweeping the file — which buys voice differentiation instead of a uniform offset. Final: sting 0.00, questions 81.7 (floor 39.8), exclamations 20.4 (band 5.3-42.6), contractions 190.6, fragopen 0.00. The file appears in no warning.
155 of 336 records are offered ZERO of their OWN topics (before and after my change alike). Not mine and not caused by me — banked so it is not rediscovered.

THE MIRROR OF THE HEADLINE DEFECT, FOUND AND MEASURED, NOT FIXED (owner call, named so it is not rediscovered): 40 infos in game/data/dialogue/topics/** are written for an actor name that NO NPC RECORD IN THE BUILD WEARS. magister 23, notary 6, dockhand 3, walker 3, scribe 2, vakh-speaker 1, smuggler 1, harbourmistress 1. Same root cause as the headline — nothing ever joined the roster in game/data/npcs/** to the `a` fields in the dialogue — and just as invisible, because a dead info does not error, it simply never gets scored. `magister` is one of the SIX archetypes in speakers.json: a whole voice slot, with calibrated fingerprint targets and its own address form ('provincial'), written for a mouth that does not exist. Its world-side counterpart is `dres-factor` (25 records). Whether the fix is to rename the actor on 25 NPC records or to alias the two in the reader is a DATA-OWNERSHIP decision, not a coverage one, so I measured it (root-coverage.mjs Q5) and left it. I did NOT silently alias another piece's voice slot.

IN PLAY, `latest rumors` IS NOT THE 65%-dull line the census reports. 321 of 336 speakers have a live settlement rumour from dialogue/rumours.json, and after the extras-dedup fix that rumour REPLACES the generic root entry. The census tool measures infoFor() alone and cannot see the supply, so 65% is its ceiling, not the played figure. Stated so nobody quotes the wrong one.
AFTER adding a `someone-in-particular` place tier: overall DULLNESS 28.9% -> 25.2%, that root's commonest line 51% -> 18%, cell-gated deliveries 736 -> 848, still 0 misplaced.

game/data/index.json regenerates via tools/analysis/data-index.mjs; it had already picked up the new file, and --check is clean. A dialogue file not in the index does not load in the browser, so this is worth confirming before any browser pass.

SUCCESSOR RE-RUN at commit 0b2d6ef (clean tree; orchestrator banked the predecessor's work): instrument still GREEN. coverage 336/336 all nine roots, dullness 25.2%, misplaced 0 of 848 cell-gated, 40 dead-actor infos reported. --self-test now 9 pass 0 fail (predecessor's file said 5; three M5 spelling/gossip assertions and an M1 full-coverage split have been added). Numbers survived the two commits that landed after they were taken.

BROWSER RUN 1 (commit 0b2d6ef, 6 browsers / loadavg 2.4): 8 pass 2 fail. BOTH FAILURES WERE THE PROBE, NOT THE WORLD, and the node census was right. C1-C5 passed on the first browser run: a merchant in Gideon who could answer NOTHING before this round answers all nine out loud; two trades in one town differ 3/3 on the self-roots and agree 2/3 on the world-roots; ONE gossip keyword; and the CONSUMPTION mutation silenced the person and restoring it gave back the identical words.

C6's FAILURE WAS A CHECK DEMANDING THAT A CORRECT ANSWER BE WRONG. It watched `services` and asserted the line must change when the speaker moves town. For a MERCHANT, `services` resolves to the `a: merchant` actor row (specificity 8) which beats the cell tier (2) — a line about the trade, not the town, and right to follow them to Thorn. The 0-misplaced figure from the node census was never in question. Rewritten to split the nine by what the reader ACTUALLY CHOSE and to carry a control: cell-gated answers must change, cell-less answers must not.

AND C6 COULD NOT HAVE BEEN WRITTEN CORRECTLY, because `Conversation.state()` reported `greeting_cell` but never `said_cell` — infoFor() has returned `cell` since the gate was turned on and NOTHING could see it. Any probe asking 'did they give me GIDEON's line?' had to match the town's name inside the prose, which passes whenever a line merely mentions the place. Added `said_cell` to state() (one line, mirrors greeting_cell, no behaviour change).

C7's FAILURE WAS THREE WRONG API FACTS IN FOUR LINES: an NPC's `pos` is the ARRAY [x,y,z] not {x,z} (so the teleport went to NaN); queueInputs events are {f, press, release} with `f` an OFFSET from the current frame, and {frame, down, up} is REFUSED by the fail-closed key check; and interact only sets `_talkPending` — talkTo runs in _afterStep, so too few frames after the press looks exactly like a reach failure. C7 now also asks all nine rather than one, and asserts the button reached the PERSON and not a prop standing near them.
next_step: re-run w1-speakers-ask.mjs with C6/C7 fixed; then the four checkers; then blog line
notes_for_successor: SHAPE DECIDED (argued in the report): generic floor per root, cell tier for the world-roots, actor rows ONLY on the three SELF-roots (duties, my-trade, background) where the answer is about the speaker. Do NOT write 11 actors x 9 roots -- that is 'everyone has a bespoke line', which closes the number and destroys the contrast the number exists to measure. Most of what I write must be FLAT: a directions line gives directions. Do not collide with W1-PROSE-R2, which owns 55-utility.json and 50-factions.json.
